# DuckDB {#sec-duckdb} [DuckDB](https://duckdb.org/) is a popular and powerful "in-process [SQL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SQL) [OLAP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Online_analytical_processing) [database management system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Database#Database_management_system)" It provides APIs in multiple languages, including R, Python, and Julia.

In practical terms, it provides a very efficient way to read, query, and write big data in R, which includes datasets that are bigger than memory.

For example, it allows lazy-reading of large datasets with optional filtering, selecting, and grouping operations before reading into memory.

@sec-dataqueryx includes examples using [duckplyr](https://duckdblabs.github.io/duckplyr/) ::: callout-note This section is a work in progress. ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(duckdb) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Loading required package: DBI ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} library(dbplyr) ``` ::: ## Installation ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} install.packages("duckdb") ``` ::: ## DuckDB API DuckDB uses the R Database Interface ([DBI](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/DBI/index.html)). Learn more about using DBI [here](https://solutions.posit.co/connections/db/r-packages/dbi/). ## Setup Connection By default, `duckdb()`'s `dbdir` argument defaults to `DBDIR_MEMORY`, which creates a non-persistent, in-memory object. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} con <- dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` duckdb is storing downloaded extensions and secrets under ~/.duckdb: ℹ /Users/sdg/.duckdb This persists across sessions and is shared with the DuckDB CLI and other clients. ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to use a temporary directory instead. ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives. ``` ::: ::: ## Settings ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} dbExecute(con, "PRAGMA enable_progress_bar;") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 0 ``` ::: ::: ## Read CSV You can directly read into data.frame, which may be best for smaller datasets: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ir <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM read_csv_auto('./iris.csv');" ) head(ir) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Sepal_Length Sepal_Width Petal_Length Petal_Width Species 1 5.1 3.5 1.4 0.2 setosa 2 4.9 3.0 1.4 0.2 setosa 3 4.7 3.2 1.3 0.2 setosa 4 4.6 3.1 1.5 0.2 setosa 5 5.0 3.6 1.4 0.2 setosa 6 5.4 3.9 1.7 0.4 setosa ``` ::: ::: For larger datasets, you can create a DuckDB table that can be queried without loading the dataset into memory: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} dbExecute(con, "CREATE TABLE iris AS SELECT * FROM './iris.csv';" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 150 ``` ::: ::: ### List tables ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} dbGetQuery(con, "PRAGMA show_tables;") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` name 1 iris ``` ::: ::: Using the R API: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} dbListTables(con) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "iris" ``` ::: ::: ## Filter ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM iris WHERE Species in ('setosa', 'versicolor')") |> head() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Sepal_Length Sepal_Width Petal_Length Petal_Width Species 1 5.1 3.5 1.4 0.2 setosa 2 4.9 3.0 1.4 0.2 setosa 3 4.7 3.2 1.3 0.2 setosa 4 4.6 3.1 1.5 0.2 setosa 5 5.0 3.6 1.4 0.2 setosa 6 5.4 3.9 1.7 0.4 setosa ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} dbExecute(con, " CREATE TABLE ir AS SELECT * FROM read_csv_auto('./data/iris.csv', delim=',', header=True); " ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 150 ``` ::: ::: ### Fetch data to data.frame ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ir = dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * from iris") head(ir) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Sepal_Length Sepal_Width Petal_Length Petal_Width Species 1 5.1 3.5 1.4 0.2 setosa 2 4.9 3.0 1.4 0.2 setosa 3 4.7 3.2 1.3 0.2 setosa 4 4.6 3.1 1.5 0.2 setosa 5 5.0 3.6 1.4 0.2 setosa 6 5.4 3.9 1.7 0.4 setosa ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} class(ir) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "data.frame" ``` ::: ::: ### Fetch data to data.table: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ir = dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * from iris") ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} class(ir) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "data.frame" ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} head(ir) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Sepal_Length Sepal_Width Petal_Length Petal_Width Species 1 5.1 3.5 1.4 0.2 setosa 2 4.9 3.0 1.4 0.2 setosa 3 4.7 3.2 1.3 0.2 setosa 4 4.6 3.1 1.5 0.2 setosa 5 5.0 3.6 1.4 0.2 setosa 6 5.4 3.9 1.7 0.4 setosa ``` ::: ::: ## Close connection When you are done working with the database, you should close the connection: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} dbDisconnect(con) ``` ::: ## Resources - [DuckDB Documentation](https://duckdb.org/docs/) - [DuckDB CSV](https://duckdb.org/docs/data/csv)
